Senses.Explanation: Literally, 'look at mind' or 'inspect mind.' The compound occurs 474 times in 84 allowed texts, but 257 hits are concentrated in the Record of the Source-Mirror. The corpus does not give it one uniform set of predicates. In the Daoxin-Niutou Farong encounter, Farong answers 'inspecting mind' when asked what he is doing; Daoxin asks, 'Who is doing the inspecting, and what thing is mind?' (觀是何人，心是何物), and Farong gives no answer. The Treatise on Breaking Appearances says, 'Only inspecting mind, this one thing, gathers all things' (唯觀心一法，總攝諸法), then asks, 'How does inspecting mind count as understanding?' (云何觀心稱之為了). Its reply distinguishes a clean mind and a soiled mind and later says, 'Inspecting mind in this way may be called understanding' (如是觀心可名為了). The Record of the Source-Mirror quotes a different direct formula: 'Inspect mind as no mind; things do not dwell on things; my mind is itself empty; fault and fortune have no owner—this is called correct inspection' (觀心無心，法不住法，我心自空，罪福無主，即是無心無數，名為正觀). Other Chan witnesses criticize particular deployments. An imperial anthology says that making silence final and 'then devoting oneself to quietly inspecting mind' is 'escaping a pit and falling into a ditch' (便務靜觀心，又所謂逃坑落塹), while its verses say, 'closing the eyes, vainly seek seeing; inspecting mind, mistakenly seek penetration' (閉目妄求見，觀心誤覓通) and 'holding mind and inspecting mind divide guest and host' (持心觀心紛主客). Huineng separately calls 'dwelling on mind and observing quiet' sickness rather than Chan (住心觀靜，是病非禪), and Linji lists dwelling on mind, looking at quiet, looking outward, clarifying inward, and congealing mind and entering settledness as contrivances. These are text-drawn criticisms of named actions; they do not supply a single imported category for the headword.
Senses.Note: The record supports the literal verbal target 'inspect mind,' followed by speaker-specific predicates and objections. The two dominant treatise witnesses are presented as claims made by those texts; their concentration of hits does not erase the independent Chan encounter and criticism witnesses. Title and table-of-contents hits were excluded.

Occurrences.Kwic: 祖問曰。在此作什麼。師曰觀心。祖曰。觀是何人心是何物。師無對便起作禮。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Record of the Transmission of the Lamp, Niutou Farong's encounter with Daoxin. The two speakers and the unanswered challenge are preserved, so the occurrence remains unkeyed.

Occurrences.Kwic: 答曰：「唯觀心一法，總攝諸法最為省要。」問曰：「何一法能攝諸法？」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Treatise on Breaking Appearances, attributed by its title to Bodhidharma. The treatise directly calls inspecting mind the one act that gathers all things; no speaker link was asserted.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問曰：「云何觀心稱之為了？」答：「菩薩摩訶薩行深般若波羅蜜多時，了四大、五陰本空無我，了見自心起用有二種差別。云何為二？一者淨心，二者染心。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The same treatise asks directly what counts as understanding through inspecting mind and supplies its own clean/soiled distinction. The wording is reported as the treatise's definition.

Occurrences.Kwic: 普賢觀云。觀心無心。法不住法。我心自空。罪福無主。即是無心無數。名為正觀。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Record of the Source-Mirror quotes an earlier text and labels the resulting formula correct inspection. It is a quotation within Yanshou's compilation.

Occurrences.Kwic: 但既入矣，又不可以默為究竟，云此一事不在語句上，便務靜觀心，又所謂逃坑落塹也。

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Imperially Selected Recorded Sayings, verse witness. It explicitly pairs inspecting mind with mistakenly seeking penetration.

Occurrences.Kwic: 持心觀心紛主客，即心即佛添名目。非心非佛又如何，箇中妙意難容說。
